components.name: Sales data import
components.detail: Reads the weekly sales export (CSV or API) into a staging table.

components.name: Weekly aggregator
components.detail: Rolls sales up by week, region and product line.

components.name: Insight summariser
components.detail: Writes a short plain-language summary of each week's movements.

components.name: Dashboard API
components.detail: Serves weekly figures and summaries to the web app.

components.name: Sales dashboard
components.detail: Weekly view with trend charts and the timing view.

mermaid:
flowchart LR
  A[Sales export] --> B[Import job]
  B --> C[(Staging store)]
  C --> D[Weekly aggregator]
  D --> E[Insight summariser]
  D --> F[Dashboard API]
  E --> F
  F --> G[Sales dashboard]

monthly_cost.assumptions: About 4,000 summary calls a month, one small database, two hosted services.

phases.name: Data access and import
phases.detail: Agree on the export format and load a sample of weekly sales data.

phases.name: Dashboard build
phases.detail: Weekly view, trend charts and the quick timing view.

phases.name: Summaries and handover
phases.detail: Add the weekly insight summaries, review with the sales team and hand over.

rationale: The brief asks for one clear weekly view of sales, inside a budget of about ten thousand dollars. A plain import, aggregate and chart pipeline covers the core need cheaply. A small language model adds the weekly summary the team would otherwise write by hand, and free-tier models keep the running cost low. The legacy SAP link is unconfirmed, so the import step stays file-based until the client confirms it.
